Priya: quick heads up — discovered a delegation edgecase: delegated API keys issued by service-token seem to inherit model access checks incorrectly. parent key allowlist only has embeddings, but delegated key can successfully call chat models. steps and logs below. assigning to eng-security and eng-runtime.

Ali: can repro locally in ~10s. repro: create parent, issue delegated subkey with allowlist=['text-embedding-*'], then call /v1/chat/completions with delegated token -> 200 + chat reply.

Priya: repro steps i ran (minimal):
```bash
# create parent key with embeddings-only allowlist
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys -d '{"scopes":["models:embeddings"], "name":"parent-emb"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer PARENT"
# issue delegated key (delegation API from service)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/delegate -d '{"parent":"PARENT","scopes":["models:embeddings"]}' -H "Authorization: Bearer SERVICE_TOKEN"
# call chat with delegated token
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer DELEGATED" -d '{"model":"gpt-open-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}] }'
```
Response: 200, model produced chat output.

Mike: do we have audit logs showing enforcement? which check returned allow? please paste the authz log lines.

Priya: pasted relevant authz log from runtime (redacted):
```
ts=2026-03-20T14:02:31Z level=info event=authz_check token_id=dk-abc123 parent_key=pk-xyz allowlist=[models:embeddings] route=/v1/chat/completions result=ALLOW reason="inherited_model_tag: gpt-open-1 matches parent-model-visibility"
```
(weird bit is reason says inherited_model_tag even though parent shouldn't allow chat)

Sarah: suspicious — looks like delegation flow is using the parent-key's model tag mapping instead of the delegated token's explicit scopes. maybe we only validate delegated token existence and then short-circuit to parent metadata for model->capability mapping.

Ali: confirmed: runtime code path for delegated tokens calls validate_token() which sets effective_scopes = token.scopes || parent.scopes. bug is `||` used instead of merge/strict-eval. delegated tokens with empty model scope fall through to parent.

Mike: KMS question: are we losing allowlist tags during wrapping/unwrapping? does wrapped metadata preserve the delegated token's scope tag or only parent tag? audit shows wrapped_key.tag=model:embeddings on parent but delegated wrapped token was missing tag.

Priya: checked key metadata in KMS: parent key has tag model:embeddings, delegated wrapped key has no model tags (we attach scopes at issuance). runtime currently prefers KMS-tag over token-scoped claim if present. that precedence feels backwards for delegation.

Sarah: mitigation options:
- immediate: revoke all delegation issuance (disable delegation endpoint) and rotate any parent keys that issued delegations in past 24h.
- short: patch runtime to prefer token.claimed_scopes when present for delegated tokens (tight check) and block fallback to parent if token.claimed_scopes non-empty.
- long: add unit + e2e test for delegation boundary (emb->chat) and add KMS metadata hygiene check at wrap time.

Priya: created a quick ACL rule we can hotfix: enforce route-model-compat(token_claims, route) before consulting parent metadata. patch ready in a branch, requesting urgent review.

Mike: also need audit/forensics: list all parent keys that issued delegations in last 30 days and run queries for chat calls authenticated with delegated tokens. Ops, can we map delegated token IDs to parent IDs in logs?

Priya: yes logs have parent_key field. sample query I used: `select * from authz_logs where parent_key is not null and route like '%chat%';` returned ~27 events in prod in last 48h.

ops-bot: Incident INC-20260320-01 created by @Priya, severity=P1, assigned to eng-security and eng-runtime. Pager duty: eng-runtime oncall paged.

Ali: will open PR with minimal guard (reject chat route if delegated token's scopes do not include chat models). tagging @mike and @sarah for review.

Sarah: good. also add an audit event when we reject a delegated token for route mismatch so we have evidence for rulings and customer notifications.

Mike: one more thought — we need to check rotation semantics: if parent key rotates, delegated tokens should remain valid only per their explicit scopes. ensure rewrap doesn't drop scope claim. coordinate with KMS team on tag preservation.

Priya: noted. I'll start a runbook item: revoke/redact delegated tokens associated with affected parents, notify customers if we see chat usage exceeding expected baseline, and add a postmortem checklist.

Ali: PR: https://git.redwood.internal/r/dep/1234 (draft) — adds strict evaluation path + unit tests. CI green locally.

Sarah: thanks team. next steps: 1) hotfix merge + deploy, 2) rotation + revoke for impacted parents, 3) full audit and customer outreach if needed, 4) follow-up postmortem. assigning follow ups in OKRs.

Priya: i'll coordinate the deploy window. marking this thread as primary thread for the incident.

Mike: ACK.

Priya: any objections to P1 -> P0 escalation if we find delegated tokens in the wild calling chat for production customers?

Sarah: escalate to P0 if we see >=5 unique customer apps impacted or sensitive data egress. otherwise stick P1.

Ali: will monitor and report back.

Priya: thanks all.
